chosen.chosen: The command name `organize-downloads`, run as `organize-downloads [--move | --undo] [folder]`, with the folder as an optional last argument.
chosen.why: T2 puts the tool's README at `organize-downloads/README.md`, so one name serves the folder and the command; long options name the move and the undo the criteria speak of, and a plain argument for the folder is how command-line tools usually take a path.

chosen.chosen: The exact lines the tool shows: `<name> -> <Kind>/` for a move, `<name> stays: <reason>` with the reasons `hidden file`, `still downloading`, `folder`, `a file of the same name is in <Kind>/` and `<Kind> is a file, not a folder`; for undo `<Kind>/<name> -> <name>`, `<Kind>/<name> not put back: <reason>` and `removed empty folder <Kind>/`; a header line naming the folder and a count line at the end.
chosen.why: The completion criterion of T1 asks that the builder takes the messages from the UX without asking; one line per entry, the same in preview and move, lets the user compare what they agreed to with what was done.

chosen.chosen: The extensions each kind holds, told by the text after the last dot, whatever its letter case; a file with no extension goes to Others.
chosen.why: AC2 names the kinds but not their extensions; the lists hold the common extensions of each kind on macOS and Linux, and ignoring case keeps `photo.JPG` with `photo.jpg`.

chosen.chosen: A file named like a kind's folder keeps the files of that kind where they are, shown as `stays: <kind> is a file, not a folder`.
chosen.why: Without it the kind's folder cannot be made without renaming or overwriting that file, which AC5 forbids.

chosen.chosen: Lines stand in alphabetical order of names, letter case aside, and in an undo the file lines come first by file name, then the removed folders by name; subfolders are listed as `stays: folder`, apart from the kinds' folders, which get no line and are not counted.
chosen.why: The user finds a file's line where they expect it and sees that each of their own subfolders is left alone as AC4 says, while the kinds' folders, being where files go, would only add a line to every run.

chosen.chosen: Undo goes back only to the last move run, once; a second undo, or one after a move run that moved nothing, shows `Nothing to undo in <folder>.`
chosen.why: AC10 speaks only of the last move run; undoing it twice would have nothing true to put back.

chosen.chosen: Errors: `organize-downloads: no folder at <path>` for a missing folder, `organize-downloads: use --move or --undo, not both` for both options, each changing nothing; `--help` shows the usage line and what each option does.
chosen.why: These are the cases a user meets by a typing slip, and the builder needs their messages; changing nothing keeps AC5.

chosen.chosen: Box kinds in the figures written as mermaid entity codes, `#lt;person#gt;`, rather than bare angle brackets.
chosen.why: Mermaid strips bare `<person>` as an HTML tag, so the kind would not show in the rendered figure the user reads on the pull request.
